newsitem.title: USA: US lawmakers to meet with DOE on heating oil.
newsitem.headline: US lawmakers to meet with DOE on heating oil.

text.p: Several lawmakers from the Northeastern part of United States are to meet later Tuesday with U.S. Energy Secretary Hazel O'Leary to discuss potential problems from low stocks of home heating oil.
Connecticut Democratic Sens. Joe Lieberman and Christopher Dodd, along with Democratic Rep. Joe Kennedy of Massachusetts in a statement said they would meet with O'Leary.

Because of tight supplies, the Energy Department has said prices for home heating oil, which is used heavily in the Northeast, will be higher this winter. It said there is a potential for price spikes if the winter is unusually cold.

Last week the Northeast lawmakers wrote O'Leary a letter that said: "Based on recent reports, we have doubts as to whether the nation's refiners have the time or capability to build a level of middle distillate inventories high enough to protect consumers in the upcoming heating season."
Kennedy also has suggested the administration sell oil from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve, and use revenue to buy home heating oil to be sold to consumers this winter.
